subject: How can I keep IDs of loci when performing PCASamples?

messages.author: eba681062e6d7098
messages.subject: How can I keep IDs of loci when performing PCASamples?
parts:
Hi Altuna,

I am attempting to find out the loadings on PC1 of each methylated CpG entered into PCASamples.

So far, I have used the following command to get PC scores for my methylbaseDB object (meth_red)

output <- PCASamples(meth_red,obj.return=TRUE)


By default this excludes the lower 50% quantile of loci. This is fine.

However, looking at output$rotation I see the loadings for each locus across all Principal Components have sequentially ordered row numbers; that is the row numbers are specific to 'output', not 'meth_red'.

Since the row numbers in the PCASamples output do not match the row numbers of the original methylbaseDB object, which contains the columns describing the chromosome and base number I need, my question is how do I transfer the locus position columns into the PCASamples output?

Many thanks,

Ian

parts:
you can do PCA yourself on the percent methylation matrix, there you will have control over filtering and you can try to retain row order or add rowids that might help you keep track of rows/columns, depending on if you transpose the matrix or not.

Best
Altuna

messages.author: eba681062e6d7098
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I keep IDs of loci when performing PCASamples?
parts:
I worked it out! Starting with a methylBaseDB object called 'meth_red'...

obj <- percMethylation(meth_red, rowids=TRUE)

rv <- apply(obj, MARGIN = 1, FUN = var) # MARGIN=1 means apply the function to rows # 'MARGIN=1' means apply the function to rows, 'FUN = var' means calculate variance

obj2 <- obj[rv > quantile(rv, probs = 0.5), ] #Creates a new methylBaseDB object containing only those rows that have a variance in the top 50% values
pca <- prcomp(t(obj2), center=TRUE, scale.=TRUE)


'pca' now contains the exact same loading scores as a PCASamples default run would, but with the added bonus of listing the loci which those loadings describe.

Thanks for the advice, Altuna, and I hope this is useful to others :)

Ian
